item.title: First attempt at an SCP: the girl with stag horns
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlight: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator pitch:
• An SCP that has minimal anomalous properties (enhanced senses, physiological abnormalities, Etc.) most of the time but it has an active time.
• During the active time it is extremely hostile and warps reality around it within a 20 Km radius.
Central Narrative: The SCP is found in a forest/cave system after several missing persons reports are filed for the area. The foundation acquires it at the end of it’s active time and it is compliant to the agents that were sent after it and it is placed in relatively low security. Exactly 11 months after the SCP is first acquired it enters its active state and breaches security.
Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reality warping effect causes the landscape to be a twisted, darkened version of the area that the SCP was found in. During its active period the SCP has a small radius that causes slowed cognitive ability
Additional Notes: Please tell me if any of these ideas boring, convoluted or stupid.

item.title: Inaccurate Extradimensional War Reenactment
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy

Elevator Pitch: A phenomenon that manifests near the locations and annual anniversaries of famous battles. Terrain and weather in the affected area reconfigure to match the original battle, and invisible and intangible entities manifest to reenact it, along with the appropriate military hardware, which is visible but still intangible. The Foundation initially thinks that these entities are ghosts, but they eventually notice that they’re sentient and aware of their surroundings, then attempts to make contact. The Foundation briefly speaks with the entities, enough to realize some humorous misconceptions the entities have about how human war works in three-dimensional space. Eventually, the entities manifest to reenact a battle that never happened. When the Foundation points this out, the entities realize they’re in the wrong universe and demanifest, never to return.

Central Narrative: The Foundation first discovers this phenomenon when it manifests near a populated area. There’s a log of notable manifestations (current list includes the Battles of Bull Run/Manassas, Hastings, Rorke’s Drift, and Megiddo, plus a prehistoric conflict between Homo sapiens and Neanderthals and a battle between the Mongols and Daevites). The log notes illustrate the Foundation’s dawning awareness of the entities’ sentience and attempts to interact, concluding with a final log of a manifestation somewhere in the Southern US that doesn’t correspond with any known battle. There are two addenda after that: one chronicling a humorous interaction between a Foundation personnel and one of the entities and one chronicling the final encounter with the anomaly, during which they realize they’re in the wrong place (“We’re in the wrong universe, you stupid idiot!”).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The bait-and-switch of anomalies that seem to be ghosts but are actually slightly confused extradimensional war-reenacters is an amusing twist. I also intend to imply or even crosslink that the nonexistent battle is the one described by SCP-592. I plan to eventually write a Tale about the universe full of faceless people described by that book and encountered in SCP-970.

Additional Notes: I’m not sure if I should have the anomalies manifest at the actual locations of the battles or on some shapeshifting island or something out in the middle of nowhere. Having them at the actual locations requires all sorts of memetic/amnestic foolery on the part of the Foundation and/or the entities to preserve normalcy, which I worry would bloat the Description and stretch suspension of disbelief.

item.title: The Tainted Saint Collection (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a Euclid-class collection of parasitic donor organs that are capable of osmotic extracellular digestion. Individual "fragments" of SCP-XXXX possess passive, non-lethal cognitohazardous properties.

Central Narrative: The Tainted Saint Collection is the first entry in a wider narrative I have planned. It's centered around the research of Dr. Lee Elliot, an ex-field agent with an interest in SCPs that can manipulate organic matter. I intend for this narrative to begin (temporally) with a different SCP, an incident report, and a Tale. However, this SCP seemed like a better place to start in practice since it's easier to pitch.

The report starts out normal, with little off-kilter details sprinkled in to breed unease. Note, I described SCP-XXXX as a collection of donor organs in the intro here, but in the article itself that information will not be revealed until the description section. By the time the reader reaches that point, I want them to be hyperaware of the danger associated with even brief contact so the reveal that they were implanted into people hits as hard as possible.

Beyond that, the bulk of the article's narrative will follow the background of each fragment individually, outlining their quirks. SCP-XXXX-B, for example, kills its hosts within a few days, whereas SCP-XXXX-A remained inside the same host for six months. At the end, I plan on including a brief interview between SCP-XXXX-A's ex-host and Dr. Elliot. Lastly, I'll include a short lab report detailing a non-lethal vivisection of SCP-XXXX-A that ended up costing Dr. Elliot his left eye. Spoiler alert: fragments of SCP-XXXX are immobile by choice, not biology.

Hook/Attention Grabber: They're carnivorous donor organs with cognitohazardous properties. I know I'd read an article about that.

Additional Notes: I have way too much experience writing formal academic prose, so my main concern is getting the lore/terminology right. I'm also wondering if anyone knows some good SCPs that introduce recurring researcher characters without making that introduction too intrusive. I don't want the article to end up feeling like it's about Dr. Elliot.

item.title: Medicine Man - first scp idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • The Medicine Man is a sculpture that activates when an individual lowers their guard or gets distracted within the statue's area of effect. The victim is unaware of this, but will see the manifestation of the sculpture's consciousness (as in "its soul"), which calls itself The Medicine Man. Once confronted with the medicine man, said individual will never be able to fully focus/concentrate again (unknowingly), which makes the individual more vulnerable to the sculpture's effect. When exposed to the statue for too long, one could enter a comatose state or develop Alzheimer's.
  • When trying to prevent an individual from totally succumbing to the medicine man by attempting to improve their ability to focus with external forces (caffeine, adrenaline injection, etc.), Medicine Man will switch said individual's consciousness with itself, trapping the individual consciousness in the statue. Medicine Man can then host a body until it finds another statue to reside in.

Central Narrative:
Medicine Man traveled from sculpture to sculpture, while leaving behind a trail of corrupted minds. This is how the foundation found him.
Inside the foundation, Medicine Man is appreciated for its vast amount of knowledge about chemistry and biology and is sometimes given a host to be interviewed by researchers.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Opposite of cognitohazard that corrupts the mind without the victim knowing, which I personally find quite creepy

Additional Notes:
I had already started a draft in the sandbox because I didn't know i needed a greenlight.

item.title: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror

Elevator Pitch: A series of interstellar radio signals make their way to earth, warning of an impending threat. After the first message, the foundation ensures no other stations can receive the signals.

Central Narrative: After determining the radio signal's origin to be extraterrestrial, the foundation sets about discovering what sent it, why it was sent, where it was sent from, what the threat is, why "protection" is no longer possible, and why it was needed. The answers to these questions are vague, with the threat remaining unknown and the senders of the radio signal also remaining unknown.

However, it is discovered that the signal originated from the Canis Major Dwarf Galaxy, and it is assumed this possible threat the senders were protecting us from likely originated from the same galaxy. This assumption is later confirmed when foundation astronomers discover an abnormal mass exiting the galaxy, with a trajectory towards earth.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures for when the mass arrives at earth, which suggest that, if the mass cannot be neutralized and is a threat to all civilisation, then a full planetary evacuation is to commence. My hope is that this will coax the reader into reading deeper.

Additional Notes: Currently N/A.

item.title: Re: PF Account Transfer
item.content:encoded:
We plan to transfer everything that's public over - all your revisions, pages, comments, etc. We'll probably end up reserving all active/contributor account names during and after the transfer. The intent would be for you to be able to reclaim your current username and hopefully not notice any differences. item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
1) Part of Doomsday's powerset is that any attack makes him add to his defenses in the form of bone spurs, much the same way your SCP grows obsidian. He's also a feral character, but where yours tend to flee and eat, Doomsday tends to attack and kill. Again, not saying to not pursue the idea based on that, especially as it looks like you're deviating far enough away from it.

[And yeah: SCP-682 is essentially the reptile version of Doomsday, but the symbology works out slightly different (more of a "we chained the monster" than "monster out to kill us".]

2) The "doctor becoming too familiar with his patient" is a standard trope, as is the "faithful worker finding problems with his object of worship". Again, not saying it's a bad thing, just be aware of the traps.

item.title: Re: A parallel world
item.content:encoded:
How are the artifacts discovered if it doesn't exist in our but instead the parallel world

The objects exist in both worlds, half of each object is in our world and the other half of each is in the other world. Think of it this way: Take 10 DVDs and glue them one on top of the other to make a thick cylindrical stack of DVDs. Now do some magic and send the bottom 5 of these DVDs to another universe which is parallel to ours but keep them linked/glued to the 5 that remain in our universe. Now when you move the stack of 5 DVDs that is in our universe, you are also moving the stack of the other 5 in this parallel world that you sent them.

Now imagine you do the same to another stack of 10 DVDs. Now you can make the "invisible" part of the two stacks touch without bringing the visible parts into contact. You'd feel resistance and you would be unable to move them closer together because their otherworldly counterparts are touching each other.

I have a draft drawing of this that I want to attach to the post, I'll try to post it here too.

were the Foundation trying to find them

I don't explain how exactly they found them but I explain how they realized that they were "special". Remember this thing in our universe looks like a granite cylinder, nothing special. But trying to rotate it and it's center of mass is not where it should be so it behaves weirdly. Additionally if you tried to move it fast with a car, it would stick with force to the back of your car as it would encounter serious resistance in the parallel world while trying to move through the thin fluid there at a high speed.

I like the Lovecraftian kind of feel to this idea,

;-)

I suggest you add some sort of story, perhaps by exploration and testing logs

I have about half of the draft describing three incidents regarding the two artifacts. First incident involves the cleaning crew hearing whispers (each one in their own language though) coming from the artifacts, and ends up with an attempt at a rational explanation. (I guess that's a bit Lovecraftian too haha)

The second incident was about sudden, apparently purposeful tugs to the objects, hinting at entities living in the other world.

The third incident is about the disks heating up due to some phenomenon on the other side. I can definitely elaborate more on these incidents if you think it needs more story.

Perhaps I could play with adding a transcript for a recorded research log? Though I'm not sure if this should be an attachment to the whole SCP or part of it. I guess an attachment, I don't think a transcript makes sense in the middle of an SCP, does it?

Is it against the rules to post a link to my draft? I saw that I should only post it if reviewers (or was it greenlighters?) ask for it.

SCP 5001 did this very well without explaining or revealing too much, leaving it to the audience to fill in the blanks instead.

I will read this now to get some ideas of what proportions of storytelling to reporting is good. Funny… I used SCP-5000 in my draft as a placeholder for my SCP. :-D

item.title: Re: First SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the review. Wish I could've responded sooner but I had stuff IRL to deal with.

To prepare for this I read a lot of the Sarkic tag here to get an idea on how sarkic magic works. I noticed that it seems that they are somehow able to replicate biomass from an original source since relatively small communities have large bioforms. The idea is that the SCP here was being trained in how to manipulate and replicate flesh but is using that power for a mundane use instead. The Karcists in particular seem to be very skilled at doing this. The idea I had is a Polish Karcist in training decided to abandon that life and becoming a proper Karcist to live a regular life. He still has the training and skill with flesh warping that you'd expect from a Karcist, but instead of sculpting flesh to create monsters he's sculpting slabs of beef and pork to feed people in his neighborhood. So an extraordinary power that's being used in a mundane way.

One detail that I forgot to mention is that I'm going to have him come to the United States after World War 1. He used the confusion of the war to escape his community. So he's doing this before modern GMOs. He's able to sell high quality meat in an immigrant community, during the great depression at one point no less. That's going to get someone's attention. I haven't decided yet on whether or not he gains the attention of the regular mob or a neo-sarkic group in the area. But either way a group of unscrupulous individuals catches wind of him and tries to extort him of money and meat.

Another idea I had was that this be something similar to SCP-2610 in that the UIU finds him first and becomes an SCP later. The wider thought is that between 2610 being in Boston and SCP-2480 being somewhere in Massachusetts there appears to be a lot of flesh warping anomalies in the same region. So it's possible the Foundation and the UIU work together to monitor sarkic and similar such anomalies in New England. He being an SCP is apart of this cooperation.

But I do see what you mean by needing to develop the abilities more. Right now the struggle is explaining enough to give an idea of what makes him special and not over explaining so it's not just "how to flesh warp your steak".

item.title: Re: (Seking Greenlight) World of the Wars
item.content:encoded:
The problem is that you're thinking middle ground. Either go big or go small, but never go middle ground.

If you build up the idea of hold-outs, you could have a series of extra-dimensional spaces that contained soldiers from other wars. The spaces could only be accessed at specific times so that the soldiers were unaware that they were even in such a space. This could create some obvious issues, especially if the decidedly warlike soldiers interacted with peaceful populations.

On the flip side, there could be a master dimension of sorts that ties all of the various wars together, and Obskuracorps has figured out how to access it. They could use this to find soldiers from previous wars as well as tech from future wars, and The Foundation needs to stop them before they figure out how to grab that future tech.

item.title: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
I've never given full critique before, so take this with a larger grain of salt that usual. Like, a big grain. Like, an entire salt lick sized grain.

+ Line Critique
- Line Critique

I'm sure a lot of this is super pedantic, so I have given each critique a pedantry rating. "Important" means I think it might be an issue, "Medium" means it could go either way, "Nitpick" means it's such a small and pedantic critique that it probably doesn't matter too much.

The temperature in its containment chamber is to be kept at a minimum of 28 degrees Celsius and no higher than 35 degrees Celsius.

I think this is a difficult line to get across with good clinical tone while still being concise. I think the thing to ask is, how specific does a researcher need to be here? If the minimum temp is 28 and the maximum is 35, why not just rephrase as:

"The temperature in the containment chamber is to be kept between 28 and 35 degrees Celsius."

This might lose a bit of information, as it might feel like the researcher could just pick whatever temperature they want. But another possibility would just be:

"The temperature in the containment chamber is to be kept at 30 degrees Celsius."

After all, I'm sure the foundation has the technology to just set a themostat and leave it at a constant temperature, not having to worry about these wide sweeps. From this, it's just implied that the temperature shouldn't swing too far away in either direction, and the lack of the word "exactly" means it's okay for it to drift a reasonable amount, as would be expected in a humanoid containment cell.

Rating: Medium

Two arms extend from center mass. It is planted in an orange ceramic pot.

Again, we're trying to convey information both precisely and concisely. Which is hard! Maybe we can get some conciseness by combining the two thoughts, and using "trunk" rather than "central mass", since we're talking about a cactus. Also, you missed a word before "central mass", probably the word "its"

"Two arms extend from its central trunk, which is planted in an orange ceramic plant pot."

Rating: Important

…the ability to levitate 2 meters in the air…

Wait, I thought it levitated 30 cm in the air, like it said at the beginning of the description? Is it 30 cm or 2 meters?

Rating: Important

…and 'swing' itself at potential threats.

I don’t see that as anomalous. If it can levitate and locomote, this is just a corollary of those two properties.

Rating: Medium

…Colt Paterson Revolver,

Revolver shouldn't be capitalized here.

Rating: Medium

…and the ability to cause explosions in quick succession.

I think this is too vague a statement to leave dangling here. What kind of explosions? At the gun, or at the things shot at? Normal guns generally don’t cause explosions outside the barrel. It's later revealed through addenda that you mean "It can fire either normal rounds or explosive rounds". That should be explained here.

Causes explosions in quick succession ≠ has the ability to fire rounds that cause things struck to explode.

Rating: Important

SCP-XXXX was initially seen…

Usually I’ve seen the verb her be “initially discovered” or something similar, “seen” feels a bit casual.

Rating: Nitpick

Encounters with SCP-XXXX have been documented in the Addendum.

There are multiple, so you should using the plural, “documented in the following addenda”

Rating: Important

NOTE: SCP-XXXX enters a Starbucks to ask for information on the whereabouts of Lana Ringle.

That’s not really a note, more of a Summary

Rating: Nitpick

SCP-XXXX moves into Starbucks, makes sounds…

It doesn’t really make sounds, right? It communicates telepathically, so shouldn’t it be transmits, or possibly is heard making sounds? I dunno, it's strange using language not meant for the anomalous to talk about the anomalous.

Also, clearing your throat is generally considered one sound. So "makes a sound" would be more appropriate here.

Rating: Nitpick

<It groans and then moves to the cashier.>

I usually see the pronouns issue around sentient SCPs avoided by just not using pronouns. Instead of “it”, just stick with “SCP-XXXX groans and moves to the cashier”

Rating: Nitpick

<Points at herself.>

For these action transcriptions, the tone could use some work. They should be separate from the text, and should probably be complete thoughts. So here, rather than “Points at herself”, you could try “The cashier points at herself”. I'll just note this one here as to not be redundant, but I'd make sure all these action transcriptions are full sentences.

Rating: Important

After SCP-XXXX left Starbucks…

Left the Starbucks

Rating: Medium

…were notified of its existence and were deployed to look for it.

Again, typical verb use for these cases would use “search for it”

Rating: Nitpick

The following video log comes from security cameras in a Walmart

In a local Walmart

Rating: Nitpick

Note: It was immediately after this incident that residents filed complaints about an unusual taste in their drinking water.

“residents began filing complaints”, since they all didn’t file them at the same time

Rating: Nitpick

SCP-XXXX immediately went to Scrankle Sales Barn in Hollister, Texas, after its earlier escape from embedded personnel.

immediately "fled" to, since "went" is a bit leisurely for the circumstances.

Rating: Nitpick

The ground shakes. A manhole cover on the main road nearby ejects from its slot, ascends to a height of approximately 5 meters vertically and lands on car, triggering its alarm.

A bit of action is lost here, and the grammar’s not perfect.

The manhole cover goes from going straight up to being in a car, like it hit it from below. The fall should take as long to read as the rise, so the action can be followed in our mind's eye. Personally I think the lack of an oxford comma contributes to this, but I'm not getting into that debate right now.

You’re probably looking for something closer to:

“The ground shakes. A manhole cover on the nearby road ejects from its slot, ascending to a height of approximately 5 meters before falling and landing on a car, triggering its alarm.”

Rating: Important

SCP-XXXX rode the horse south where it found Lana Ringle and the hooded figure…

Two ideas here, riding and finding, so you could add a comma after “south”

Rating: Nitpick

…falling to the ground and wrestling it.

It takes two to tango. "Wrestling with it."

Rating: Medium

- Line Critique
+ Larger Scale Critique
- Larger Scale Critique

Special Containment Procedures

ConProcs can be difficult to write depending on the idea, because while they're generally necessary for the rigid format of the sight (and not including them can incur insta-downvotes), they can end up being just padding if they don't fit with the story you're trying to tell. I can tell by the length here that, if it wasn't a requirement, you probably wouldn't have any. I truly think there could be a bit of foreshadowing to the 3rd addendum revelation put in here, something subtle. I'm not sure exactly what that could look like, but it might be a nice way to use the space.

Description

Besides my nitpicks, the description is fine. Probably the low point of the document for me, maybe because of all the nitpicks I found, but of course this is just setup for the logs to come.

Addenda

Humor is subjective. Some people may think this is funny, some might not, but all I can tell you is how I feel. I think a lot of this is damn funny. If you fix up the action transcription issue, I would love most of it even more. I like the gradient in ridiculousness felt between them, it really ramps up to the final conflict, which then feels both real and ridiculous.

The only thing that stuck out at me as odd was the second video log of the first addendum, the action there felt a bit hard to follow overall. Prixors infiltrates a store, a customer gets the gun, and an explosion blows Prixors and the gun back out. Firstly, I feel like Prixors says way too many words between noticing the customer reaching and the customer pulling the trigger. Just makes this moment feel less real, like the customer is waiting to pull the trigger to cut him off, all which ignoring the talking cactus and staying focused on a gun they found? Wait, and how does the video transcriber know the customer thinks it's a toy? Did they interview them?

Anyway, we're outside now, drawing a crowd. We're drawing a crowd, the agent tries to dissipate it, and Prixors notices our PoI. Prixors levels his gun at him (again, it's a bit hard to read because the action transcriptions aren't full sentences), and fires into the crowd. The action then follows Prixors and the chase, which is strange because we just fired a gun into a crowd of civilians. What happened to them? Are they screaming and running in circles, adding to the chaos? Because they're not referred to again, it feels like they just… didn't react, and got out of the way. Which is weird.

- Larger Scale Critique

Overall, I think if this was tightened up with some really close reading and style nitpicking, it would be an easy upvote from me. I don't know if everyone will appreciate that final addendum, but I sure did. I though it was a pretty well choreography action scene, built up well, and with a nice but still ambiguous reveal. The ending left me with questions, but good questions. Questions that you might want to hint at the answers too in the ConProcs and Description, but it's fine how it is. Pleas let me know in the future when you've gotten enough feedback and worked on it enough that you feel comfortable posting!

item.title: Re: The Grand Conspiracy
item.content:encoded:
First, this isn't technically an SCP; there's nothing anomalous about it. It's just a video.

Good point, maybe this could be a tale instead, or maybe even an explained SCP, anyways, I decided to make it so the Foundation just left it up so people would ignore it and forget it after a while.

Your last paragraph has an interesting idea, but I don't want to make it too serious. If the people narrating has solid proof of the theory, that would make the audience more inclined to believe it, both in and out of the universe, so perhaps someone working as a janitor of the Foundation, or a prison inmate who notices the disappearance of his fellow inmates, and makes up the theory.

I don't want it to feel, "No way! The Foundation was behind all of that?!" More of a "Wait, could the Foundation actually have done that?" Not enough evidence to convince people, but enough for people to wonder about it.

item.title: Re: SCP that preys on sex predators (Trigger Warning: Description of an Abuser and his crimes)
item.content:encoded:
I get the idea of having sexual predators becoming prey animals to an even more destructive force, but this doesn't sound like it's going to be

A) sensitive to the survivors of sexual assault, or

B) anything more than a mary-sue/X-man trope with a bit of sexual exploitation sprinkled on for spice

Topics like this are hard to write, even for experienced and established authors. Most people just stay away from these topics in the modern era of SCP authorship, and for good reason. I get the allure of wanting to explore darker aspects of human nature, and at least this idea isn't putting the reader in the shoes of someone that wants to commit these atrocious acts.

That being said, humanoids in general are also difficult to write because they have the conjoined issue of being both something we need to relate to in order to engage with the story, while also embodying characteristics that are inherently unrelatable.

Frankly, none of the way this has been presented gives me any confidence that this will be anything more than what I've already said.

item.title: An Old Theater (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): Commonplace SCP article layout, with Interviews, Exploration Logs, and addendums.

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation contains an old theater once an entire town's population seems to disappear into it on re-opening night. Inside, the Foundation finds spatial anomalies; flesh-eating and mind-controlling fungi; and a creature hewn together from corpses that desperately wants to exit the building to "follow it's directive".

Central Narrative: The article's Special Containment Procedures seemed to be overly detailed and specialized for an Euclid, until the head researcher revealed to have lived in that town and that they knew just what happened the first time the theatre opened (interviews). The fungi within is observed to interfere with electronic equipment within the building, and it seems mainly to grow from the creature’s blood and secretions. When d-class are sent to investigate with less specialized transmission equipment, they discover a seemingly endless series of waiting rooms, storage areas, backstages, and stages filled with decaying props. The props and hints towards the play performed vary wildly from room to room, and the one room the d-class seem to find but not explore is a basement, from where the creature emerges and kills most of the d-class in the exploration party; those who survived ended up proving the contagious capabilities of the fungus inside and were terminated.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The creature within stitches all those who it manages to catch onto itself, through a redacted procedure observed through drone observation (exploration logs). And it is stated that there was one time the creature actually managed to breach containment, and in the time it took Foundation personnel to find out where the creature had gone, it managed to decimate the entire population of a city, level several buildings, and almost open a portal into an unknown dimension possibly filled with creatures alike it. The creature’s sudden increase in capabilities when outside containment proved that the building’s anomalous properties seem to aid in the containment of the creature.

Additional Notes: The Article’s series of addendums let it be known that the creature, the last times it’s been seen by personnel within the building, has been covered in water or has left humid footprints. After analyzing the remains of this water, it is found to be that of the abandoned town’s sewer system. The petition to include the sewer system into the containment procedure, or to force its collapse through demolition charges was left pending.

item.title: How Long Can We Wait? - Cognitohazard SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

Essentially, there are 3 parts to this SCP:
- The first is a cognitohazardous message. Once you read it, it will stay in your mind, slowly growing in you consciousness, eventually replacing all other thoughts, shutting down your motor functions, and killing you, as you will forget how to breathe. This cognitohazard can also be spread, and creates a strong desire in the infected to visit the second part of this skip.
- The second is an anomalous creature. It is located in a pit, and anyone who approaches or enters the pit will be filled with an extremely strong hatred towards the creature, and a powerful desire to end its life. The foundation believes, however, that if this creature were to die, it would result in an end-of-the-world scenario.
- The final part is a site, believed by the foundation to be the origin of the apocalypse should the creature ever be killed. the site is marked by a ring of 5 statues, 1 resembling the creature in the pit, and the other resembling redacted creatures that the foundation has already encountered. Additionally, every month, a creature spawns at this location, which must immediately be terminated by foundation personnel.

+ Rest of the post
- hide

[Central Narrative:
There isn't exactly a narrative per se, but the reader will slowly uncover more information about the SCP, and how the different parts of it relate together. Essentially, the message will draw the victim to the creature in the pit, and once they get there they will be compelled to kill the creature, beginning the apokalypse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I feel like the cognitohazard is a fairly unique premise, and the chain of events that could so easily lead to the apokalypse.

Additional Notes:
Considering going more in-depth through addendums as to who the other 4 statues are. They would be deceased creatures that the foundation has already encountered, implying that all five must be killed in order to free some cosmic being, and the creature in the pit is the last remaining "lock" if you will.]
